subject: chemical
audience: FE Chemical candidates and chemical engineering students
title: The Evaporator That Removed 750 kg/h of Water
featured_title: THE EVAPORATOR THAT REMOVED 750 KG/H OF WATER

presentation.challenge: The feed was 1000 kg/h at 10 wt% solids. Concentrating to 40 wt% left only 250 kg/h liquid product.

practice.primary_question: How does a nonvolatile-solids balance determine product and vapor flow in an evaporator?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Assuming a 40 wt% product means 40% of the feed remains as liquid product.

case_dna.target_misconception: Concentrating a 1000 kg/h feed to 40 wt% solids means the liquid product flow is 400 kg/h.
case_dna.why_plausible: Forty percent looks like a natural fraction of the 1000 kg/h feed.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: The feed contains only 100 kg/h nonvolatile solids. If those solids are 40% of the product, product flow is 100/0.40=250 kg/h, leaving 750 kg/h water vapor.
case_dna.corrected_model: For a nonvolatile solute, balance the solute first; it fixes the concentrated-product flow.

problem_statement: An evaporator receives 1000 kg/h of solution containing 10 wt% nonvolatile solids. Water is evaporated, and the liquid product contains 40 wt% solids. Assume no solids leave with the vapor. A quick estimate says the product flow is 400 kg/h because the product is 40% solids. Determine the actual liquid-product and vapor flow rates.

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The product was 40 wt% solids. It was not 40% of the feed flow.
gates.prompt: Which conserved component fixes the liquid-product flow?

options.label: Balance nonvolatile solids first: FzF=PxP
options.reason: All feed solids remain in the liquid product.

options.label: Set product flow to 40% of feed flow
options.reason: Forty percent is the product composition, not the fraction of feed retained.

options.label: Split solids between product and vapor
options.reason: The problem states the solids are nonvolatile.

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Run the evaporator
gates.result: The liquid product is 250 kg/h and water vapor is 750 kg/h.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the solids balance
gates.hint: Feed contains 100 kg/h of nonvolatile solids.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: The nonvolatile component closes the balance

cards.text: 100 kg/h is 40% of a 250 kg/h liquid product, leaving 750 kg/h water vapor.

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the evaporator note
report: C3. Therefore product flow is 400 kg/h.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: It confuses product composition with the fraction of feed remaining.

evidence_choices.label: 100 kg/h solids / 0.40 = 250 kg/h product
evidence_choices.reason: This follows from the conserved nonvolatile-solids balance.

correction.template: The liquid product is {product} kg/h and evaporated water is {vapor} kg/h.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Concentrate the same feed to 50 wt% solids
gates.constraint: Keep the same 1000 kg/h feed at 10 wt% nonvolatile solids.

options.label: Product flow becomes 200 kg/h and vapor flow becomes 800 kg/h
options.reason: 100/0.50=200 kg/h product; the rest is evaporated water.

options.label: Product flow becomes 500 kg/h
options.reason: That would contain 250 kg/h solids, more than enter with the feed.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply a nonvolatile-solids balance
gates.prompt: A 500 kg/h feed contains 20 wt% solids and is concentrated to 50 wt% solids. What is the product flow?

options.label: 250 kg/h
options.reason: That would correspond to 40 wt% solids.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the evaporator balance
gates.confirmation: I confirm that evaporator product flow should be determined from the conserved nonvolatile component before calculating vapor flow.

items.label: What failed
items.value: Product composition was mistaken for a feed-flow fraction.

items.label: What was missed
items.value: Only 100 kg/h of nonvolatile solids enter.

items.label: Corrected model
items.value: Use the solids component balance, then the overall balance.

seo.seo_title: Evaporator Mass Balance: Why 1000 kg/h Feed Gives 250 kg/h Product | FE E-062
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Chemical Case E-062: a 1000 kg/h feed at 10 wt% solids concentrated to 40 wt% gives 250 kg/h product and 750 kg/h water vapor.
seo.excerpt: Product concentration is not the same as the fraction of feed retained. The nonvolatile-solids balance determines the product flow.
seo.direct_answer: The feed contains 100 kg/h nonvolatile solids. At 40 wt% solids, product flow is 100/0.40=250 kg/h. The remaining 750 kg/h leaves as water vapor.

faqs.q: How do you solve an evaporator material balance with nonvolatile solids?
faqs.a: Balance the solids first, then use the overall mass balance for the vapor flow.

faqs.q: How much water is evaporated in this case?
